turns.content: Triangle ABC has side lengths AB=4, BC=6, and AC=8. Use the law of cosines to find cos(angle ABC).
Place B=(0,0) and A=(4,0), with C above the x-axis. Find the exact coordinates of C.
The square ABQR is drawn outside the triangle. With this orientation, determine the coordinates of Q.
The square BCST is also exterior to the triangle. Determine the coordinates of T in the same coordinate system.
Use the geometry of the two external squares to find BQ and BT and to relate angle QBT to angle ABC.
Check that angle relation directly from the vectors BQ and BT, including the sign of its cosine.
Use the resulting side lengths and included angle to compute QT in exact radical form, and verify the squared distance from the coordinates.
